verdict.rationale: Lovable's Git sync documentation states that you can clone the repo, edit and commit locally in your IDE, and push, with the changes syncing back into Lovable automatically. That covers the whole story: local editing with your own tooling plus round-trip sync to the platform. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the local-to-platform round-trip sync, and documented detail on conflict handling.

support.subject: As a developer, I can work on the app locally with my own editor and tooling and push changes back to the platform

citations.quote: Work locally in your IDE. Clone the repository, edit and commit locally, and push. Your changes sync back into Lovable.
Git sync connects a Lovable project to a repository you own on GitHub or GitLab, and keeps the two in sync automatically
you can export and sync your project to GitHub: back up your code, review changes in pull requests, work locally in your IDE, test features on branches, and deploy outside Lovable
